texts.preamble: Dalpat Singh (I)(Fir141615Burari) vs Yograj (Uiic) on 18 October, 2024 In The Court Of Dr. Ruchi Aggarwal Asrani Presiding Officer, Mact-01 (Central) Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi. Dlct010019602016 Mact No. : 57197/2016 Fir No. : 1416/2015 Ps : Burari u/s : 279/338 Ipc
texts.facts: The DAR revealed that a Road Traffic Accident took place on 30.10.2015 at about 07:00 PM in front of Sangam Vihar Gali No. 3, Main Jharoda Pusta Road, Near Jharoda Chowki, Jharoda, Burari, Delhi wherein the petitioner, . The accident took place with a vehicle i.e. Motorcycle bearing registration No. DL14 SA 0767 driven and owned by respondent no.1, Sh. Yograj and insured with Dalpat Singh (I)(Fir141615Burari) vs Yograj (Uiic) on 18 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65696587/ 1 respondent no.2, United India Insurance Co. Limited. BRIEF FACTS OF THE CASE: 2. The brief facts that have emerged from the DAR are that on 30.10.2015, the information of an accident was received at P.S. Burari vide DD No. 33 PPJ. ASI Bharat Ratan along with Ct. Vishwendra went to Hindu Rao Hospital where the injured Dalpat Singh was found under treatment vide MLC No. 7281/15. The alleged history on the MLC was mentioned as RTA and patient had come to casualty himself for medical examination. On the date of the accident, the injured Dalpat Singh did not give any statement due to which, the DD entry was kept pending. 3. Thereafter, the injured Dalpat Singh had appeared at the police station Burari on 16.11.2015 and gave a written complaint with respect to the accident in question wherein he had stated that on 30.10.2015 at about 7.00 P.M., he was going to his home on his scooter via Sant Nagar and Jharoda Pusta and when he reached near Gali no. 3, Sangam Vihar in front of Main Jharoda Pushta Road, one motorcycle bearing registration no. DL 14SA 0767 while ridden by its driver in very high speed, rashly and negligently came from the wrong side and hit his scooter due to which he fell down on the road along with his scooter. The motorcycle rider immediately fled away from the spot. The injured stated that he also stood up and went from the spot of the accident by riding his scooter, however, when he reached in front of Hansraj College, he felt pain in his right arm, both the knees and ears. He noticed that water was oozing out from his left ear. He sat there only and dialed at 100 number and after some time, he went to Hindu Rao Hospital for his treatment. He stated that on the date of accident, he was not able to give his statement and therefore, he had come to the police station with his written complaint. He prayed that strict legal action be taken against the driver of the offending vehicle. On the basis of MLC of the injured and his written complaint, the offence under Section 279/337 IPC was found to have been committed and accordingly, the FIR No. 1416/15 was registered under section 279/337 IPC at P.S. Burari. 4. During the course of investigation, the IO prepared the site plan. The accidental scooter was seized by the IO and deposited in Malkhana. He got the mechanical inspection of the scooter of the injured conducted. Notice under Section 133 M.V. Act was served upon the registered owner of the offending vehicle who appeared at the police station along with the offending vehicle. The IO arrested the driver of the offending vehicle, however, since the offence was bailable, he was released on bail on furnishing of bail bonds. The IO seized the offending vehicle as well as the documents pertaining to the offending vehicle and got the same verified from the concerned authorities. Later, both the vehicles were released on superdari. The IO collected the MLC of the injured after final opinion as per which, the injury was found to be 'grievous'. Therefore, section 338 of IPC was added in the FIR. After completion of the investigation, chargesheet under section 279/338 IPC was filed against the driver Yograj and DAR was filed before this Tribunal on 04.05.2016. 5. Written statement on behalf of respondent no.1 was filed on 10.01.2017. Written statement on behalf of respondent no.2 insurance company was filed on 01.07.2016. ISSUES FRAMED Dalpat Singh (I)(Fir141615Burari) vs Yograj (Uiic) on 18 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65696587/ 2 6. Relief. EVIDENCE 7. To prove his case, the petitioner examined himself as PW-1, and Sh. Shri Kishan, Notice Server from Income Tax Department, Ministry of Finance, Delhi as PW-2. The respondents did not lead any evidence. 8. The Petitioner filed the Form XIV. Financial statement of the petitioner has been recorded. Final arguments were heard on behalf of the petitioner and respondent no. 2. The factum of accident: 12. In this matter to prove the occurrence of the accident as well as the rashness and negligence on the part of the driving of offending vehicle by respondent no.1, the petitioner (PW-1) in his evidence by way of affidavit Ex. PW1/A had deposed as under:- "1. That the deponent is the petitioner in the present DAR/injury claim and being well aware of the facts, is competent to swear this affidavit in evidence. 2. That on fateful day i.e. at about 07:00 PM on 30.10.2015, when the injured/petitioner was returning to his home from Sant Nagar, via Jharoda Pushta and when he reached ahead of Chowki Jharoda, in the mean time an offending vehicle i.e. motorcycle bearing No. DL-14SA-0767 came from the wrong side at a very high speed, most rashly and negligently in a zig-zag manner and hit the deceased as a result of which the deceased fell down on the road and dashed to the nearby footpath due to which he got severe internal bodily injuries particularly in the knees and some fluid mixed with blood also came out from the right ear. 3. That the accident took place due to rash and negligent driving on the part of the respondent no. 1 (driver), who drove the offending vehicle without observing traffic directions and came from the wrong side at a very high speed, rashly, negligently, carelessly, recklessly and in a zig-zag manner without observing traffic rules and safety of the public at large. 4. That due to this accident the deceased received multiple grievous injuries on his all parts of body as per the medical records/MLC and treatment records. 5. That the injured taken to Hindu Rao Hospital, where the MLC was conducted. That the petitioner sustained injuries due to the accident caused by the respondent no. 1 and due to the alleged accident the deponent/petitioner forced to shell for a sum of Rs.2,50,000/- on account of medical treatment, Rs.1,00,000/- on account of transportation to get the better treatment, Rs. 50,000/- on account of special diet, Dalpat Singh (I)(Fir141615Burari) vs Yograj (Uiic) on 18 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65696587/ 4 and Rs. 2,00,000/- on account of loss of income during the treatment period/bed rest, Rs. 1,50,000/- on account of deployment of persons to handle the business of the deponent almost a year, and it is not out place to mention here that the deponent has suffered mental pain & agony, loss of enjoyment of life, loss of income, lots of harassment, inconvenience apart from the loss of capacity to earn well since then due to the said accident. 6. Since, the petitioner was the sole bread earner of his family at the time of the said accident and therefore the deponent is entitled to receive the damages/compensation from the respondents whom are liable to pay the same. 7. That the deceased was engaged in the business of ready made garment and running his shop in the Kamla Nagar Market and was earning handsomely to the tune of Rs. 35,000/- per month and he was contributing & maintaining the entire family. The family members of the deponent, including the deponent, having been suffered great pain, agony, mental torture and shock due to the said accident and all the members were making efforts to help me out to comes out from the said trauma. The loss cannot be compensated in terms of money, however, the deponent is claiming just compensation to the tune of Rs. 25,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Lacs only) on account of the grievous injuries sustained in the said accident and suffered huge loss on account of pain & suffering, enjoyment of life, loss of income, loss of future prospectus, loss of future pecuniary benefits and other special and general damages as admissible/permissible under the law. 7. That an FIR got registered against the respondent no. 1 vide FIR no.1416 of 2015 dated 16.11.2015, u/s. 279/337/338 IPC with the police station Burari, Delhi and later the IO of the case has also filed the DAR before the Hon'ble Court and final charge sheet has also been filed before the Ld. MM having the proper jurisdiction of the criminal trial. 8. That the respondent no. 1 was the driver of the offending vehicle and he was driving the said offending vehicle under the instructions and control of the respondent no. 2 and the vehicle was insured with the respondent non. 3 thus all the respondents are jointly and severally liable to make the payment of compensation to the deponent in the sum of Rs. 25,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Lacs only) along with 18% PA interest. Therefore, the petitioner/ injured Dalpat Singh shall be entitled to Rs. 44,047.93/- towards medical expenses. Coming to the aspect of loss of income, the petitioner Dalpat Singh claimed that he was self employed as proprietor of Readymade Garments and property dealer and was earning Rs. 25,038/- per month. He has also filed his ITR as per which in the year 2015-16, his annual income was Rs. 3,00,460/- which means that he was earning Rs. 25,038/- per month. Therefore, it is held that the monthly income of the petitioner/injured Dalpat Singh at the time of the accident i.e. on 30.10.2015 was Rs. 25,038/-. Further, the petitioner has claimed that he was not able to work for 05 months but he has not filed any such document on record to prove that he was not able to work at for 05 months. However, keeping in view the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner as well as the disability certificate, it is held that the petitioner shall be entitled to the Loss of Income for 05 months i.e. Rs.25,038/- x 5 = Rs. 1,25,190/-. The petitioner/injured has claimed Rs. 50,000/- under the head pain and suffering. The petitioner has claimed Rs. 25,000/- under the head mental shock. Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65696587/ 15 29. The petitioner has claimed Rs. 30,000/- under the head conveyance charges but there is no cogent evidence for the same. However, considering the nature of injuries suffered by the injured/petitioner, this Tribunal is of the opinion that petitioner must have incurred some expense on conveyance. Attendant charges: 30. The petitioner has claimed Rs. 30,000/- under the head attendant charges. Considering the nature of injuries suffered by the injured/petitioner, this Tribunal hereby grants compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards attendant charges. Attendant charges for business: 31. The petitioner has claimed Rs. 35,000/- under the head attendant charges for business on the ground that he could carry on his business only with the help of support staff. Compensation for loss of amenities: 32. The petitioner/injured has claimed Rs.25,000/- under this head. The petitioner has not filed anything on record to prove his claim to the extent of Rs.25,000/- towards loss of amenities. However, taking into account the injuries suffered by him and also noticing the disability suffered by him, Rs. 25,000/- is awarded to the petitioner under this head. Future loss of income: 33. The petitioner Dalpat Singh has claimed loss of future earning to the extent of Rs. 3,71,000/- in his Form XIV. It has already been established that the petitioner has suffered 15% permanent disability in relation to his right left limb. Therefore, the functional disability of the petitioner is assessed at 7.5% in relation to the whole body for the purposes of calculating the compensation. The income of the petitioner has been assessed as Rs. 25,038/- as on the date of accident. Special Leave Petition (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014, date of decision - 31.10.2017). In the present case, the interest was stopped vide order dated 19.08.2019 till the conclusion of PE which was closed on 31.08.2024. Therefore, it is held that the petitioner shall be entitled to interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of DAR i.e. 04.05.2016 till 19.08.2019 and then again from 31.08.2024 till realization. The Financial Statement of the petitioner/injured was recorded by this Court/Tribunal. As per the said statement, the monthly expenses of his family are approximately Rs. 25,000/- to 30,000/- per month.
texts.arguments: Further, procedural approach adopted by an accident claims' tribunal mirrors that of a civil court (National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Smt. Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2009 ACJ 287). In civil proceedings, the establishment of facts hinges on a preponderance of probabilities, rather than being bound by the strict rules of evidence or the higher Dalpat Singh (I)(Fir141615Burari) vs Yograj (Uiic) on 18 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65696587/ 3 standard of beyond reasonable doubt, as required in criminal cases. In Bimla Devi & Ors. v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors (2009) 13 SC 530, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India that negligence must be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view must be adopted in reaching a conclusion. On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for respondent no. 2 argued that while it is the case of the petitioner that the accident in question had occurred on 30.10.2015 but the FIR was recorded on 16.11.2015. Ld. Counsel for respondent no. 2 further argued that it was the petitioner who was rash and negligent in driving his vehicle. He also argued that the offending vehicle was impounded on 29.01.2016 and as per its mechanical inspection report dated 05.02.2016, no fresh damage was found in the offending vehicle. The deposition of PW-1 as to the manner of the accident and the driving of the offending vehicle in a rash and negligent manner by the respondent no. 1 is categorical. He has specifically deposed that the offending vehicle had come from the wrong side in very high speed in rash and negligent manner and hit his scooter due to which he fell down on the road and sustained injuries. He has also denied the suggestion that he was rash and negligent and the accident occurred due to his fault. Furthermore, in view of filing of DAR containing the charge-sheet for the offences u/s 279/338 IPC and other relevant documents against the respondent no. 1 and in terms of the judgment in the case of National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, respondent no. 1 Yograj (driver-cum-owner of the offending vehicle) is held to be negligent on the basis of preponderance of probability. It has already been concluded in the preceding paragraphs while deciding the issue no. 1, Dalpat Singh (I)(Fir141615Burari) vs Yograj (Uiic) on 18 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65696587/ 7 that the petitioner had suffered grievous injury and he has permanent disability of 15 % in relation to his right lower limb. 20. Before proceeding further to decide the present issue, it would be apposite to encapsulate the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in its guiding lamp post judgment for ascertaining just compensation in road vehicular injury cases. In the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Ors. (2011) 1 SCC 34, Hon'ble Supreme Court held as under: "General principles relating to compensation in injury cases 4. The provision of The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (`Act' for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The Court or tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. (See C. K. Subramonia Iyer vs. T. Kunhikuttan Nair - AIR 1970 SC 376, R. D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Ltd. - 1995 (1) SCC 551 and Baker vs. Willoughby - 1970 AC 467). 5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following : Pecuniary damages (Special Damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising : (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Ltd. - 2010(10) SCALE 298 and Yadava Kumar v. D.M., National Insurance Co. Ltd. - 2010 (8) SCALE 567). Dalpat Singh (I)(Fir141615Burari) vs Yograj (Uiic) on 18 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65696587/ 10 9. An appropriate multiplier needs to be ascertained as per judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in matter of Sarla Verma Vs. DTC 2009 ACJ 1298 SC according to age of the injured/victim. Thus, as on the date of accident i.e. 30.10.2015, the petitioner was aged 45 years and 01 month. Thus, he was more than 45 years old and less than 46 years of age on the date of the accident. Accordingly, the Multiplier of fourteen (14) is taken for purposes of calculating the loss of income of the petitioner (Reliance is placed on the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC), the future prospects of Dalpat Singh shall be 25% as he was self employed and between the age bracket of 40-50 years at the time of accident on 30.10.2015. 35. 18 (i) The bank shall not permit any joint name to be added in the saving account or fixed deposit accounts of the claimants i.e. saving bank accounts of the claimants shall be an individual saving bank account and not a joint account. (ii) Original fixed deposit shall be retained by the bank in safe custody.
